There is **no link** between the MMR vaccine and autism. The scientific consensus is definitive:

- **Numerous large-scale studies** across multiple countries involving hundreds of thousands of children have found no association between the MMR vaccine and autism.

- The **1998 study** by Andrew Wakefield that suggested such a link was [retracted in 2010](https://www.bbc.com/news/health-12615329) after it was revealed serious methodological flaws and ethical violations. Wakefield lost his medical license.

- Major health organizations including the **WHO**, **CDC**, **National Academy of Medicine (Institute of Medicine)**, and **American Academy of Pediatrics** have all concluded there is no causal link.

- Research from [Denmark (Hviid et al., 2019)](https://annals.org/aim/fullarticle/2734582-mmr-vaccine-autism-and-autism-spectrum-disorder) with over 650,000 children, including high-risk subgroups, found no increased autism risk.

The original concerns have been thoroughly discredited by the weight of evidence. Autism is understood to have strong genetic and developmental origins that begin *in utero*, before any childhood vaccinations occur.
